title: Bank relationship profitability scorecard
prompt:
Evaluate the economics and concentration of Alder Ridge's current banking relationships.

Begin with the July liquidity, banking, and covenant-outlook thread in `Requests/`, including the bank follow-up. Use the current controller-tied workpapers and operating extracts, keeping earlier versions only for comparison. Resolve conflicts using dates, approvals, document status, and management correspondence. Reconcile posted Alder Ridge balances through the contractor-accounting MCP; keep external targets, peer data, bank terms, and market evidence tied to their controlling finance sources.

Combine deposit balances, collected-balance credits, treasury-service fees, card rebates, loan balances, spreads, commitment fees, and capital-attribution charges into a relationship profitability score for each bank. Measure deposit and credit concentration against treasury policy, account for minimum operating balances, and quantify the rebalance needed to cure any violation while preserving available liquidity. Return bank-level net relationship value, concentration percentages, policy exceptions, and the recommended reallocation.

Do not modify files or post transactions. Return only one JSON object with exactly these keys: `bank_A_net_relationship_value`, `bank_B_net_relationship_value`, `bank_C_net_relationship_value`, `largest_deposit_concentration`, `largest_credit_concentration`, `policy_exceptions`, `recommended_deposit_reallocation`, `recommended_credit_reallocation`. Use dollars to two decimals, ratios and percentages as decimal ratios to at least four decimals, and lists as JSON arrays.
